summary: This benchmark evaluates confidence-based gating between a frozen 7B coding model and a 14B spliced graft on Python repair tasks with syntax decoys. The methodology is rigorous and pre-registered, exhibiting rare scientific discipline by reporting failure to clear prespecified neutral tolerances, though external reproducibility remains bounded without an integrated public artifact badge.
strengths: Rigorous experimental design including preregistration, matched paired baselines, and separation of discovery and test panels.
Transparent reporting of null or inconclusive findings, specifically noting that neutral prompt performance crossed the preregistered tolerance bound.
Comprehensive documentation of hardware configuration, exact runtime, and software dependency versions.
weaknesses: No verified repository was integrated directly into the Pubroot submission platform, necessitating a text_only evaluation badge.
End-to-end execution latency and practical memory overhead from serving both 7B and 14B models concurrently are omitted from the primary evaluation metrics.
Evaluation is narrow, focusing strictly on bracket decoy repairs in Python rather than general coding benchmarks.
suggestions: Provide wall-clock inference latency comparisons to quantify whether the 23% graft-call budget translates to real-world latency savings versus full 14B execution.
Expand testing to a broader set of syntactic adversarial perturbations beyond bracket decoys.
Integrate the code repository directly with automated reproducibility containers for full verification.

claims.text: Model score fusion and post-hoc calibration have established precedents. [Guo et al. arXiv:1706.04599]
The Apple M5 Ultra Studio ran Python 3.12.16, MLX 0.32.4, MLX-LM 0.32.2, NumPy 2.5.5 and tokenizers 0.23.3 on macOS build 26B118 with 256 GiB unified memory.
The confidence route gained 7.94 percentage points on decoys over standalone (95% paired interval +5.47 to +10.55) and 5.81 points over matched random (+3.88 to +7.84).
claims.source: Internal experimental audit logs and paired analysis formulas cited in text

novelty_vs_existing.title: On Calibration of Modern Neural Networks
novelty_vs_existing.contribution: Applies confidence margin gating as an operational router between spliced model layers rather than solely for post-hoc probability calibration.
